newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end 1.6 pct lower as Telecom plunges 23c.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end 1.6 pct lower as Telecom plunges 23c.

text.p: * New Zealand share index ends sharply lower
* Telecom sold on back of profit downgrades
* NZ employment data goes practically unnoticed
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
328 -7 * NZSC cap index -6.70 at 5,106.97
369 -5 * Volume NZ$72 million. Futures -23 at 1,178
709 -23 * Other movers - -15 -15
New Zealand shares closed sharply lower on Tuesday with leading stocks, particularly Telecom, savaged by offshore selling.
"We have had a soft market for a couple of weeks and it seemed to come to a head today -- there has been heavy selling across all the leaders," said Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index shed 38 points or 1.6 percent to end at 2,339.94, with Telecom down 23 cents to $7.09.
"There's been a lot of broker downgrades," Koller said of Telecom's decline.
He said the market leader had been getting some bad press lately, with competitor Bell South initiating legal proceedings against Telecom for alleged price and service bundling.
After the close, Telecom announced it would soon commence with its NZ$1 billion share buyback, which brokers described as "opportune" timing.
"I think they've done it because they wanted to do something to arrest the rapid decline," Koller said. "Nobody wants to see their share price getting savaged like that."
Brokers noted the sale of an offshore portfolio and said it was an indication that foreign investors were becoming more bearish on New Zealand equities.
About 2.7 million Carter Holt Harvey shares worth some $10 million had crossed early in the session, the forester ending seven cents weaker at $3.28.

Brokers said the market had taken little notice of employment data released this morning which showed New Zealand's unemployment rate had fallen to 5.9 percent in the December quarter, its lowest level in more than eight years.
